title: Kepler: Mysterium cosmographicum (Tübingen, 1596), Astronomia nova (1609) and Harmonices mundi (Linz, 1619)

license.payload: Per item, recorded in origin.items. Johannes Kepler died in 1630; the three printings (1596, 1609, 1619) are in the public domain everywhere. Internet Archive: the Astronomia nova copy (Smithsonian Libraries) is marked 'Not in copyright'; the Harmonices mundi copy (Smithsonian Libraries) carries no rights statement; the Mysterium copy (ETH-Bibliothek Zürich, from e-rara) carries the Public Domain Mark 1.0. The Latin Wikisource transcription of the Harmonices mundi is CC BY-SA 4.0 for the site's contributions, redistributed under the same licence.

normalization: Originals as fetched under original/: Internet Archive scans with their OCR layers, the Wikisource HTML as served with its revision ids. text/<slug>.ocr.txt is the Archive's OCR with line endings normalized; text/harmonices-mundi-ws.txt is the Wikisource parser output reduced by code, its three pages joined under '=== <title> ===' headings. The Mysterium scan (68 MB) is held by reference (identifier, file, size and md5), its OCR layer copied. No text was corrected by hand. The OCR reads long s as f and breaks ligatures; the loci are phrases it read correctly.
scope: Held: the three Latin works named in the ruling, each in its first printing: the Mysterium cosmographicum of 1596 (held by reference, OCR copied), the Astronomia nova of 1609 and the Harmonices mundi of 1619 (scans copied), with the partial Latin Wikisource transcription of the Harmonices mundi beside the scan. Not held: the second edition of the Mysterium (Frankfurt, 1621, with Kepler's notes; Archive prodromusdissert00kepl, found and not seated); the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek copy of the 1596 printing (11218183bsb, 131 MB); the Copenhagen copies of the Astronomia nova and the Harmonices (den-kbd-pil-20008609-001, 656 MB; den-kbd-pil-210090002470-001, 391 MB), too large and duplicating the Smithsonian copies; the other works (Ad Vitellionem paralipomena, Dioptrice, Epitome, Tabulae Rudolphinae, Somnium), which are on the Archive and outside the ruling. No modern edition (Gesammelte Werke, 1937–) is held: it is in copyright.

why_seated: Kepler's three books are one argument carried through a life: the solids that should fix the spheres, the war on Mars that broke the circle into the ellipse, and the harmonies in which the periods and the distances were finally joined. The seat holds each book as it was first printed, so that the third law can be looked for where Kepler set it, in book V of a work on the music of the world.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-30: "and then an ea-corpora seating... Einstein, Gödel, Tesla, Copernicus, Galileo, classical Arabic mathematicians... what is in the public domain, and what else? and just to be perverse lets seat the promised Klee notebooks with them"; to the proposed set: "yes, thats a good set".
seating: EA-CORPORA-30, the thirtieth seating: the exact sciences and Klee's Bauhaus notebook, 2026-10-30
queued: Mysterium cosmographicum, second edition (Francofurti: Erasmus Kempfer for Godefridus Tampachius, 1621), with Kepler's notes: Internet Archive prodromusdissert00kepl (20 MB, University of Toronto), found and not seated; the ruling names the first printing

cross_references.in_this_seating: 30/04 copernicus (De revolutionibus), 30/05 galileo (the Sidereus nuncius, to which Kepler answered with the Dissertatio cum nuncio sidereo, 1610), 30/07 newton, 30/11 archimedes-ptolemy (the Almagest; the appendix to Harmonices mundi compares the work with book III of Ptolemy's Harmonics, which is not seated).
